Based on the suspicious images of the spinous processes of the C7 and D1 vertebrae in the X-rays of the cervical and dorsal vertebrae (Figure 1), cervicodorsal computerized tomography was performed (Figure 2). The spinous process fractures of the C7, D1 and D2 vertebrae were diagnosed as Clay-shoveler's fractures. The patient was treated with a cervical collar for 1.5 months. in_text_mentions: After further testing, including a four-view cervical spine radiograph, a fracture of the C7 spinous process was identified (Figure 1). The neural foramina were patent, and there was a loss of normal cervical spine curvature, but no other abnormalities were noted. Based on all the above findings, the final diagnosis was confirmed to be a C7 spinous process fracture.
